gloss: to look forward to; to eagerly await

definitions.gloss: to look forward to; to eagerly await
definitions.explanation: to anticipate something with pleasure and excitement

examples.japanese: {週末|しゅうまつ}を{楽|たの}しみにしている。
examples.english: I'm looking forward to the weekend.

examples.japanese: お{会|あ}いできるのを{楽|たの}しみにしています。
examples.english: I look forward to meeting you.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}たちは{遠足|えんそく}を{楽|たの}しみにしていて、{前|まえ}の{晩|ばん}は{眠|ねむ}れなかったらしい。
examples.english: The children were so looking forward to the field trip that they apparently couldn't sleep the night before.

notes:
One of the most common expressions for anticipation in Japanese. Almost always appears in the ている form ({楽|たの}しみにしている) to express an ongoing state of looking forward to something. The polite form {楽|たの}しみにしています is a standard closing phrase in business emails and conversations.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {楽|たの}しみにしている: am looking forward to
- {楽|たの}しみにしています: look forward to (polite)
- {楽|たの}しみにしております: look forward to (humble/formal)
- {楽|たの}しみにしていてね: look forward to it! (casual)
- {楽|たの}しみにお{待|ま}ちしています: looking forward to it (polite business)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {待|ま}ち{遠|どお}しい: can hardly wait — emphasizes impatience and the feeling that time is passing too slowly
- わくわくする: to be excited — focuses on the excited feeling itself rather than anticipation
- {心待|こころま}ちにする: to eagerly await — more literary and formal

USAGE:
In email sign-offs, {楽|たの}しみにしています is equivalent to English "I look forward to..." and is appropriate in both business and casual correspondence.
